subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should ordinary plugin runtime code be allowed to call plugin-registered Gateway methods, and what API and authorization shape should carry plugin caller identity?
rationale: The implementation substrate exists, but choosing between raw dispatch, allowlisted Gateway calls, or typed plugin service/capability contracts changes the public Plugin SDK and Gateway security boundary.

options.title: Design an authorized SDK contract
options.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep HTTP-route dispatch only
options.body: Decline ordinary plugin-to-plugin Gateway calls and keep Gateway dispatch reserved for authenticated plugin HTTP routes plus existing curated runtime helpers.

options.title: Expose raw Gateway dispatch
options.body: Add a generic method-string caller and accept the larger security and compatibility surface as an explicit maintainer-owned product decision.

recommendation.title: Design an authorized SDK contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The current route-scoped dispatch contract and Plugin SDK boundary history point most strongly to this account for the API/security decision.
